title: Generative AI for Computer Vision - Week 6 Assignment 6
subject: Generative AI for Computer Vision

questions.question: 1. What is the main goal of a generative model?
options: To generate new data similar to the training data
To reduce the number of classes
questions.correctAnswer: To generate new data similar to the training data
questions.explanation: Generative models learn the underlying true data distribution p(x) in order to sample and generate new data instances that closely resemble the training distribution.

questions.question: 2. What does Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) try to find?
options: Parameters that make the observed data most likely
questions.correctAnswer: Parameters that make the observed data most likely
questions.explanation: Maximum Likelihood Estimation estimates model parameters by selecting values that maximize the probability (likelihood) of observing the given dataset.

questions.question: 3. What is density estimation used for?
options: Estimating the probability distribution of data
questions.correctAnswer: Estimating the probability distribution of data
questions.explanation: Density estimation involves constructing an estimate of an unobservable underlying probability density function based on observed data.

questions.question: 4. What is an autoregressive model?
options: A model that predicts the current value using previous values
A model that only processes images
A model that does not use previous information
A model used only for data compression
questions.correctAnswer: A model that predicts the current value using previous values
questions.explanation: An autoregressive model uses the chain rule of probability to predict each subsequent variable conditioned on all previously generated/observed values.

questions.question: 5. PixelCNN is mainly used for:
questions.explanation: PixelCNN is a generative autoregressive neural network that generates images sequentially pixel by pixel using masked convolutions to model dependencies.

questions.question: 6. In PixelRNN, the name "RNN" refers to:
questions.explanation: PixelRNN uses recurrent neural networks (such as Diagonal BiLSTM or Row LSTM) to model sequential pixel dependencies during image generation.

questions.question: 7. What does spatial context in an image refer to?
options: Information about the relationships between nearby or different regions in an image
questions.correctAnswer: Information about the relationships between nearby or different regions in an image
questions.explanation: Spatial context captures geometric and positional relationships between adjacent pixels, visual patches, or semantic entities across an image.

questions.question: 8. Image captioning aims to:
options: Generate a textual description of an image
questions.correctAnswer: Generate a textual description of an image
questions.explanation: Image captioning bridges computer vision and natural language processing to produce natural language descriptions describing the contents of an image.

questions.question: 9. What is the main purpose of attention in image captioning?
options: To reduce the image file size
To focus on relevant parts of an image while generating a caption
questions.correctAnswer: To focus on relevant parts of an image while generating a caption
questions.explanation: Attention mechanisms allow an image captioning model to dynamically focus on relevant spatial regions of the image corresponding to each generated word.

questions.question: 10. A Fully Visible Belief Network (FVBN) is a type of:
questions.explanation: A Fully Visible Belief Network (FVBN) is an autoregressive generative model where all variables are observed and their joint distribution is factorized via conditional probabilities.
